definition_zh: 当前的；现行的；水流；气流；电流
definition_en: happening or existing now, or a continuous flow of water, air, or electricity
core_image: 河水贴着石岸不停向前推，表面却看不出在动
scene: 河中央的水一刻不停地把木筏往下游推。 The current pulled the raft downstream.
sceneCN: 这里 current 指「水流」（第 1 个义项：水的流动）；句意是水流把木筏往下游拖。

senses.title: Flowing water or air
senses.definition: a continuous flow of water or air in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 水或空气朝一个方向持续流动
senses.example: A strong current runs under the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 桥下有一股强劲的水流。
senses.why: Water in motion carries whatever floats on it.
senses.whyCN: 流动的水会带走漂浮在它上面的一切。

senses.title: Electric flow
senses.definition: the flow of electric charge through a wire or circuit
senses.definitionCN: 电荷在导线或电路中的流动
senses.example: The current was cut for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 电流被切断了两个小时。
senses.why: Electricity behaves like water, so it borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 电的行为像水，于是借用了同一个词。

senses.title: Happening now
senses.definition: existing or happening at the present time
senses.definitionCN: 在当前时刻存在或发生的
senses.example: The current price is too high for us.
senses.exampleCN: 目前的价格对我们来说太高了。
senses.why: What is running now is the version that counts today.
senses.whyCN: 此刻正在跑的，才是今天算数的那一版。

intro.en: Current comes from Latin currere, to run, through Old French corant, running.
intro.cn: current 源自拉丁语 currere（跑），经古法语 corant（正在跑的）进入英语。

items.en: Currere meant to run, and water was said to run.
items.cn: currere 意为跑，水也被说成在跑。

items.en: Currens described anything in motion or in use.
items.cn: currens 形容一切在动、在用的东西。

items.en: Corant named the running flow of a stream.
items.cn: corant 指溪流奔涌的水。

items.en: Current entered English for moving water and moving time.
items.cn: current 进入英语，既指流动的水，也指流动的时间。

items.en: Science gave the word to electricity in a wire.
items.cn: 科学把这个词用到了导线里的电上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the curr- stem, and the meaning group names things that exist at this time.
note.cn: 形近组共享 curr- 词干，近义组列出此时存在的事物。

entries.definition: a small dried grape used in cakes
entries.definitionCN: 做糕点用的小葡萄干

entries.definition: the money a country uses
entries.definitionCN: 一国使用的货币

entries.definition: at the present time
entries.definitionCN: 在目前

entries.definition: existing or happening now
entries.definitionCN: 现在存在或发生的

entries.definition: already there at this time
entries.definitionCN: 此刻已经存在的

entries.definition: still continuing and not finished
entries.definitionCN: 仍在继续、尚未结束的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a river pushing a raft and end with the price on today's tag.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从推着木筏的河水开始，落到今天标签上的价格。

normal.en: A current carries what floats, without asking.
normal.cn: 水流带走漂浮的东西，从不事先询问。

normal.en: Electricity borrowed the word because it also runs.
normal.cn: 电借用了这个词，因为电也在跑。

normal.en: The current price is merely the one running at this hour.
normal.cn: 当前价格，不过是这个钟点正在跑的那个价。

normal.en: Current affairs are events still moving, not yet settled.
normal.cn: 时事就是还在流动、尚未落定的事。

normal.en: If it is happening now, it is current.
normal.cn: 如果它此刻正在发生，它就是当前的。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf spinning downstream in a fast channel.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子在急流里打着转往下游去。

abstract.en: Picture a wire humming with a flow you cannot see.
abstract.cn: 想象一根导线嗡嗡作响，里面是看不见的流动。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag changed just this morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一张今早才换过的价签。

examples.en: The current swept the small boat toward the rocks.
examples.cn: 水流把小船冲向岩石。

examples.en: Do not touch the wire while the current is on.
examples.cn: 通电时不要碰那根电线。

examples.en: The current plan needs more money.
examples.cn: 当前的计划需要更多钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 current 记成「正在跑的」：curr 是跑，-ent 是正在，正在跑的水是水流，正在跑的价是现价。

root: 源自拉丁语 currere（跑、流动），经古法语 corant 进入英语；本义是「正在流动的」，由水的奔流引申为时间的当下，再引申为电流。

sensesIntro.en: From water in motion, to charge in a wire, to the version of things that counts today.
sensesIntro.cn: 从流动的水，到导线里的电荷，再到今天算数的那一版。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river pushing everything on its surface forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条河把水面上的东西不断向前推。

branches.en: The first picture is water moving in one direction.
branches.cn: 第一幅画面，是朝一个方向流动的水。

branches.en: Electric charge moves in the same way, so it takes the same name.
branches.cn: 电荷也这样移动，于是用了同一个名字。

branches.en: Time also runs, so what is running now is current.
branches.cn: 时间也在跑，所以此刻在跑的就是「当前」。

branches.en: Water and electricity share one word for flow.
branches.cn: 水和电共用了一个表示流动的词。

branches.en: A live wire and a live issue are both current.
branches.cn: 带电的导线和当下的议题，都叫 current。

intro.en: Current belongs to the curr- family, where running grows into rivers, wires, and the present hour.
intro.cn: current 属于 curr- 这一族，「跑」长成了河流、导线和眼前的时辰。

latinIntro.en: The Latin currere, to run, stands under current, currency, and recur.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 currere（跑）是 current、currency 与 recur 共同的根。

The currency fell against the dollar.
items.exampleCN: 这种货币对美元贬值了。

a flow moving against the main one
a hidden flow beneath the surface
items.example: An undercurrent of anger ran through the room.
items.exampleCN: 房间里流动着一股暗藏的怒气。

items.example: Two concurrent meetings split the staff.
items.exampleCN: 两个同时召开的会议把员工分成了两半。

items.example: The pain may recur in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这种疼痛冬天可能再犯。

items.example: The curriculum was revised this year.
items.exampleCN: 课程体系今年做了修订。

definition_zh: 学术的；学业的；纯理论的；学院派的；普通学科的；以学术见长的；大学教师、学者
definition_en: relating to study, research and teaching at a university, or existing only in theory rather than in practice
core_image: 深夜图书馆的一张桌子，一摞书、一支笔和一盏不肯关的台灯
scene: 开学第一周，宿舍楼下的公告栏贴满了课程和考试安排。 The academic year begins in early September.
sceneCN: 这里的 academic 是「学业的、学校的」（第 2 个义项：与学校学习安排有关）；句意为学年在九月初开始。画面里有公告栏、课程表和刚返校的学生。

pos.zh: 形容词：学术的；学业的；纯理论的；学院派的

collocations.zh: 纯理论的；与实际无关的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「学业上；学术上」
同源名词，义为「学院；研究院；专科学校」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「院士；学会会员」
同源名词，义为「学术界；学术圈」

senses.title: Relating to scholarly research
senses.definition: connected with serious study and research, especially at a university
senses.definitionCN: 与严肃的学习和研究有关，尤指大学里的研究
senses.example: Her academic research focuses on how children learn to read.
senses.exampleCN: 她的学术研究关注儿童如何学会阅读。
senses.why: The word starts from the name of the grove where Plato taught, so its first job is to mark whatever belongs to that world of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是柏拉图授课那片园子的名字，所以它最本职的工作就是标示「属于那个研究世界」的东西。

senses.title: Relating to school study and results
senses.titleCN: 学业的：与在校学习有关
senses.definition: connected with study, lessons and results at a school or college rather than with sport or social life
senses.definitionCN: 与学校或学院的课程、学习和成绩有关，而非体育或社交生活
senses.example: The academic year begins in early September.
senses.exampleCN: 学年在九月初开始。
senses.why: Once the word belongs to the school, it naturally covers the calendar and the marks of school life, not only research in a library.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词属于学校，它自然就覆盖了学校生活里的日历与分数，而不只是图书馆里的研究。

senses.title: Only true in theory, not in practice
senses.definition: of a question or argument, having no practical effect because the real decision has already been made
senses.definitionCN: 指问题或争论没有实际影响，因为真正的决定早已作出
senses.example: Whether the rule is fair is academic now that the contract is signed.
senses.exampleCN: 合同都签了，这条规则公不公平已经只是理论问题。
senses.why: What lives only in books has no weight in the street; a question with no practical consequence is confined to the study.
senses.whyCN: 只活在书里的东西在街上没有分量；一个不产生实际后果的问题，就被关进了书房。

senses.title: Dry and bookish in style
senses.titleCN: 学院派的：拘泥书本、脱离实际
senses.definition: of writing, art or thinking, correct but dry, showing more study than life
senses.definitionCN: 指写作、艺术或思想正确却干枯，书卷气多于生活感
senses.example: The film was praised abroad but called academic at home.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片在国外受好评，在本国却被说成学院派。
senses.why: The same belonging to the study becomes a criticism when the study is cut off from the street: too much book, too little life.
senses.whyCN: 同样一种「属于书房」的属性，一旦书房与街道隔绝，就变成批评：书太多，生活太少。

senses.title: A university teacher or researcher
senses.definition: a person who teaches or does research at a university, used as a countable noun
senses.definitionCN: 在大学任教或做研究的人，作可数名词使用
senses.example: She is a young academic with two books to her name.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位年轻学者，已经出过两本书。
senses.why: From the adjective describing the world of study, English made a noun for a person who lives in that world.
senses.whyCN: 从描述「研究世界」的形容词出发，英语造出一个名词，专指生活在这个世界里的人。

senses.title: Of caps, gowns and ceremonies
senses.definition: relating to the traditional dress and ceremonies of universities, such as gowns and caps
senses.definitionCN: 与大学的传统服饰和仪式有关，如学位袍和学位帽
senses.example: The graduates posed for photos in full academic dress.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业生们穿着全套学位服拍照。
senses.why: The oldest sense of belonging to a place of learning survives most visibly in its costume, where the tradition is worn on the body.
senses.whyCN: 「属于学府」这一最古老的含义，最显眼地保存在服装上：传统被穿在了身上。

senses.title: Of subjects taught for their own sake
senses.definition: of school subjects such as history or physics, studied for knowledge rather than for a trade
senses.definitionCN: 指历史、物理这类以求知为目的、而非为职业训练设置的学科
senses.example: The school offers a strong academic curriculum alongside its sports program.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校除了体育项目，还提供扎实的学科课程。
senses.why: If a subject belongs to the world of study rather than to a workshop, it is called academic, and the word then labels a whole curriculum.
senses.whyCN: 一门科目如果属于研究的世界而不属于车间，就被称为 academic；这个词于是用来标示整类课程。

senses.title: Devoted to learning, of a person or family
senses.titleCN: 以读书治学见长的（人、家庭）
senses.definition: of a person, family or institution, valuing books, study and scholarship above practical or sporting success
senses.definitionCN: 指人、家庭或机构重视读书治学，胜过实际事务或体育成绩
senses.example: She grew up in an academic family where dinner talk was about books.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一个书香家庭长大，饭桌上的话题总是书。
senses.why: When a whole household is oriented toward study, the adjective stops describing a topic and starts describing a way of life.
senses.whyCN: 当一个家庭整体朝向读书治学，这个形容词就不再描述某个话题，而开始描述一种生活方式。

intro.en: Academic goes back to the name of the grove outside Athens where Plato taught, and from there to every school.
intro.cn: academic 可追到雅典城外柏拉图授课的那片园子的名字，再从那里走向一切学校。

items.en: Akademeia was the name of a grove and gymnasium near Athens, associated with the hero Akademos. The origin of the name itself is uncertain.
items.cn: Akademeia 是雅典附近一片园林与体育场的名字，与英雄 Akademos 有关；这个名称本身的来源不确定。

items.en: Akademikos meant 'of the Academy', the school Plato founded there; it described members and teachings of that circle.
items.cn: Akademikos 意为「学园的」，即柏拉图在此创办的学派；它形容该学派的成员与学说。

items.en: Latin academia named both the place and the philosophical school, and kept the word alive through learned writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 academia 既指那个地方，也指那个哲学学派，并通过学术写作把词保存了下来。

items.en: English borrowed academy in the sixteenth century, and academic followed as the adjective for things belonging to it.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 academy，随后 academic 作为「属于它的」形容词出现。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective also became a noun for a university teacher, and gained its mildly critical sense of 'out of touch'.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个形容词又变成指大学教师的名词，并获得「脱离实际」这一略带批评的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Greek name behind the word; the near-meaning group holds words about study, theory and teaching.
note.cn: 形近组共享这个词背后的希腊名称；近义组收与学习、理论、教学有关的词。

entries.definition: A school or society for a special field, such as an art or military academy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院、研究院、专科学校」，如艺术学院或军校。

entries.definition: The world of universities and research, taken as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学术界、学术圈」，指大学与研究构成的整体世界。

entries.definition: A member of a learned academy or society.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「院士、学会会员」，指学术团体或学会的成员。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in terms of study or school results.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「学业上、学术上」，用于说明在学习或成绩方面。

entries.definition: Showing careful study and deep knowledge; describes a person or a piece of work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有学者风范的、学术性的」，多形容人或著作严谨有学问。

entries.definition: Relating to teaching and learning, often with the aim of helping people learn.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「教育的、有教育意义的」，范围比 academic 更宽。

entries.definition: Based on ideas rather than practice; closest to the 'purely academic' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「理论的」，与 academic 的「纯理论」一义最接近，但完全不涉及学校。

entries.definition: Relating to schools or to the medieval method of academic debate; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「学校的、经院式的」，语气正式，常用于中世纪学术辩论的语境。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek place name behind the word and the collocations it really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词背后的希腊地名，以及它真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Akademeia was the grove where Plato taught: academic means belonging to that world of study.
normal.cn: Akademeia 是柏拉图授课的那片园子：academic 就是「属于那个研究世界」。

normal.en: academy is the place, academic is the adjective, academia is the whole world of it.
normal.cn: academy 是那个场所，academic 是形容词，academia 是整个学术圈。

normal.en: academic year is the school calendar, a fixed phrase worth learning whole.
normal.cn: academic year 指学年，是值得整体记住的固定说法。

normal.en: academic performance is the standard phrase for marks and results at school.
normal.cn: academic performance 是表示在校成绩的标准说法。

normal.en: purely academic means it only matters in theory, as in a purely academic question.
normal.cn: purely academic 表示只在理论上重要，例如纯理论的问题。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp still on in an empty library: someone is awake because a question is not finished.
abstract.cn: 想象空图书馆里还亮着一盏灯：有人醒着，因为一个问题还没想完。

abstract.en: The same word praises and mocks: it praises depth of study and mocks distance from life.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能赞美也能嘲讽：赞美钻研的深度，也嘲讽与生活的距离。

abstract.en: A grove became a school, a school became a university, and a university became a way of life.
abstract.cn: 一片园子变成一所学校，一所学校变成一所大学，一所大学又变成一种生活方式。

examples.en: He left his job to pursue an academic career in biology.
examples.cn: 他辞掉工作，去追求生物学方面的学术生涯。

examples.en: Her academic performance improved a lot after she changed schools.
examples.cn: 转学之后，她的学业成绩提高了很多。

examples.en: Whether the delay was legal is now an academic question.
examples.cn: 这次延期是否合法，如今已只是个理论问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡德米」——阿卡德米的书房里堆满书，讲的是学术与学业。

root: 希腊语 Akadēmeia「雅典城外的学园」，相传与英雄 Akademos 有关，名称本身的来源不确定；柏拉图在此办学，遂有 Akadēmikos「学园的」，经拉丁语 academia 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Academic begins with one place of study and spreads outward: to research, to school results, to pure theory, to a dry style, to the people, the gowns, the subjects and the families of that world.
sensesIntro.cn: academic 从一处读书的地方开始向外扩散：学术研究、学校成绩、纯理论、干枯风格，以及那个世界里的人、礼服、学科与家庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp burning late over a desk of books inside a place of study.
core.cn: 核心意象：学府里一张书桌，灯亮到很晚。

branches.en: THE RESEARCH: whatever belongs to serious study and publication.
branches.cn: 研究线：属于严肃学习与发表的东西。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: the calendar, the marks and the subjects taught there.
branches.cn: 学校线：学年安排、成绩以及在校所教的科目。

branches.en: THE STUDY CUT OFF: what has no practical effect, or has too much book and too little life.
branches.cn: 书房隔绝线：不产生实际后果的东西，或书太多、生活太少的东西。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND DRESS: the teachers, and the gowns that make the tradition visible.
branches.cn: 人与服饰线：大学教师，以及让传统看得见的学位服。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: a whole family oriented toward books and learning.
branches.cn: 家庭线：整个家庭以读书治学为中心。

intro.en: Academic is a Greek place name turned adjective, and its family keeps the shape of the original school.
intro.cn: academic 是由希腊地名转成的形容词，其词族保留着那所学园最初的形状。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form academia carried the Greek word into European learning; the Greek name itself is the oldest recorded layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 academia 把这个希腊词带进欧洲的学术传统；希腊语名称本身是最早有记录的层次。

items.example: The name belongs to a place, not to a root meaning study.
items.exampleCN: 这个名字属于一个地点，而不是一个意为「学习」的词根。

items.example: The adjective first described Plato's followers.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词最初描述柏拉图的追随者。

items.example: Latin kept the word alive in learned writing.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语在学术写作中把这个词保存下来。

items.example: The academy opened in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这所学院在十六世纪开办。
它由 academy 构成 academic。

items.example: The stem carries the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载着整个词族。

definition_zh: 制造；生产；捏造；制成品；制造业
definition_en: to make goods from materials, usually in quantity, and also to invent an excuse or a story
core_image: 老厂里，工人把熔化的金属倒进模具，冷却后取出齿轮毛坯
scene: 老厂里，工人把熔化的金属倒进模具，冷却后取出齿轮毛坯。 They manufacture the gears from scrap steel rather than from new billets.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「用原料加工出成品」（第 1 个义项：把材料制成物件）；句意为他们用废钢而不是新钢坯来制造这些齿轮。图中可辨识物件：熔炉、模具、齿轮毛坯、冷却水槽；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Make goods from materials
senses.definition: to work raw materials or parts into finished objects
senses.definitionCN: 把原料或零件加工成成品
senses.example: They manufacture the gears from scrap steel rather than from new billets.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用废钢而不是新钢坯来制造这些齿轮。
senses.why: The Latin phrase behind the word means made by hand, so the verb begins as making an object out of material.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁短语意为「用手做成」，因此动词最初就是把材料做成物件。

senses.title: Produce in quantity
senses.definition: to make goods in large numbers by an organised process
senses.definitionCN: 通过有组织的流程大量制造商品
senses.example: The plant manufactures a million bottles a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂每月生产一百万只瓶子。
senses.why: Once making is organised in a factory, quantity becomes the point, and the verb carries that scale.
senses.whyCN: 一旦制作在工厂里被组织起来，数量就成了要点，动词也就带上了这种规模。

senses.title: Assemble components into a whole
senses.definition: to put together bought-in parts into a finished unit
senses.definitionCN: 把外购零件组成一台完整设备
senses.example: The workshop manufactures frames and buys the rest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个车间自制车架，其余部件外购。
senses.why: Making a whole from parts is still making, even when most parts arrive finished.
senses.whyCN: 用零件做成整体仍算制作，即使大多数零件送来时已是成品。

senses.title: Produce a substance in the body
senses.definition: to generate a substance naturally, as an organ or a cell does
senses.definitionCN: 如器官或细胞那样自然生成某种物质
senses.example: The liver manufactures bile and releases it into the gut.
senses.exampleCN: 肝脏合成胆汁并把它释放到肠道。
senses.why: A living organ makes a substance the way a workshop makes a product, so biology borrowed the verb.
senses.whyCN: 活体器官制造一种物质，正如作坊制造产品，因此生物学借用了这个动词。

senses.title: Invent an excuse or evidence
senses.definition: to create something false and present it as if it were true
senses.definitionCN: 编造不实之物并当作真的呈现
senses.example: He manufactured an alibi before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他在面谈之前编造了一个不在场证明。
senses.why: The sense grows from the same idea: something is made out of nothing and put forward as real.
senses.whyCN: 这层意思出自同一观念：某物从无中被做出来，并被当作真的拿出来。

senses.title: Goods, in the plural
senses.definition: products of industry, as opposed to raw materials
senses.definitionCN: 工业产品，与原材料相对
senses.example: The country exports manufactures rather than raw ore.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家出口制成品而不是原矿。
senses.why: The verb's product becomes a noun, and economists use the plural for made goods as a class.
senses.whyCN: 动词的产物变成名词，经济学家用复数形式指作为一大类的制成品。

senses.title: The industry, as a noun
senses.definition: the activity or trade of making goods, taken as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 制造商品的活动或行业整体
senses.example: Manufacture of cloth once paid half the town's wages.
senses.exampleCN: 布匹制造曾支付了全镇一半的工资。
senses.why: The uncountable noun names the activity itself, which is how the word stands for an industry.
senses.whyCN: 不可数名词指活动本身，这个词由此代表一个行业。

senses.title: Churn out something worthless
senses.definition: to produce something quickly and in volume with little care
senses.definitionCN: 以很小的用心快速大量产出
senses.example: The studio manufactures hit songs on a yearly schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工作室按年度排程批量炮制热门歌曲。
senses.why: When quantity is all that matters, the same verb turns critical: making becomes mere turning out.
senses.whyCN: 当数量成为唯一要紧的事，同一个动词就带上批评意味：制作沦为「出货」。

intro.en: Manufacture came through French from the Latin phrase for made by hand, and its senses spread from handwork to factory goods to invented stories. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语「用手做成」的短语，词义从手工制品扩到工厂商品，再扩到编造的故事。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manus meant 'hand'; its deeper root is reconstructed, so source uncertain below Latin.
items.cn: manus 意为「手」；其更深词根属重构形式，故拉丁语以下来源不确定。

items.en: Facere meant 'to make, to do'; its pre-Latin root is also reconstructed.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、制作」；其在拉丁语之前的词根也属重构形式。

items.en: The phrase meant 'made by hand', describing work of skill as opposed to what grows by itself.
items.cn: 这个短语意为「用手做成」，指凭技艺完成的工作，与自然生长之物相对。

items.en: French manufacture carried it into English in the seventeenth century for things made by hand and for the making of them.
items.cn: 法语 manufacture 在十七世纪把它带入英语，指手工制品及其制作。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the verb moved to factory production; the sense of inventing something false is older and rests on the same image of making.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，动词转向工厂生产；编造不实之物的意思更早，且基于同一「做出来」的意象。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same family in other grammatical roles; group two holds verbs for making or inventing something.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词的其他词类形式；第二组是表示「制作」或「编造」的动词。

entries.definition: The agent noun for the company that carries out the making.
entries.definitionCN: 施动名词，指执行制造的企业。

entries.definition: The process or the industry, with no object and no doer named.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或行业，不点明对象与施动者。

entries.definition: A building where goods are made; it comes from the same Latin verb of making, through a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 制造商品的建筑，同出拉丁「制作」动词，但走的是另一条名词路径。

entries.definition: From faber 'smith, craftsman', not from facere: it means putting parts together, or a lie.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 faber「工匠」，而非 facere：指把部件组装起来，也指谎言。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for producing anything, with no hint of factories or quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指做出任何东西的日常动词，不含工厂或数量的意味。

entries.definition: To bring forth goods, crops or results; it covers farming and energy as well.
entries.definitionCN: 产出商品、农产品或结果，也涵盖农业与能源。

entries.definition: To build a structure from parts, or to invent a story; it shares the second sense of the entry but not its first.
entries.definitionCN: 用部件搭建结构，或编造故事；与本词共用第二个义项，但不用第一个。

entries.definition: To fit components together, which is one stage inside manufacturing.
entries.definitionCN: 把零件接合起来，是制造内部的一个阶段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: 'Hand' plus 'make': the Latin phrase meant made by hand, and the verb kept the idea of turning material into an object.
normal.cn: 「手」加「做」：拉丁短语意为用手做成，动词保留了把材料变成物件的意思。

normal.en: The family runs manufacturer, manufacturing, manufactured and the adjective for what can be made.
normal.cn: 同族词包括制造商、制造业、制成的，以及表示可制造的形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark both sides: manufacture goods, manufacture parts, manufacture an excuse.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出两面：制造商品、生产零件、编造借口。

normal.en: Making a true thing and making a false one are the same act with different material.
normal.cn: 造真东西与造假东西，是同一个动作换了材料。

normal.en: In economics the plural means made goods, and the uncountable form means the industry.
normal.cn: 在经济学里，复数指制成品，不可数形式指制造业。

abstract.en: Picture molten metal settling into the shape of a gear.
abstract.cn: 想象熔化的金属沉入齿轮的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a story assembled from spare parts, then told as fact.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用零碎部件拼成的故事，随后被当作事实讲出。

abstract.en: Picture a conveyor that never stops, and a shelf nobody inspects.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从不停下的传送带，和一个无人检查的货架。

examples.en: The firm manufactures its own sensors rather than buying them.
examples.cn: 这家公司自己制造传感器，而不是外购。

examples.en: A country that manufactures little imports almost everything.
examples.cn: 制造业薄弱的国家几乎什么都要进口。

examples.en: He manufactured a reason for leaving that nobody believed.
examples.cn: 他编了一个没人相信的离开理由。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「manu（手）+ fact（做）+ ure」——用手做出来的 → 制造；转而指「做出来的话」→ 捏造

root: 拉丁语中表示「手」的名词与表示「做」的动词构成「用手做成」的短语，经法语成为一词；两个词根更早的来源均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one making: material becomes an object, quantity becomes the aim, parts become a unit, a body makes a substance, a lie is made, the products become a noun, the activity becomes an industry, and finally speed replaces care.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次「做」展开：材料变成物件、数量成为目标、零件成为整机、身体合成物质、谎言被做出来、产品变成名词、活动变成行业，最后速度取代了用心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: molten metal poured into a mould and lifted out as a gear blank.
core.cn: 核心意象：熔化的金属被倒进模具，取出时已是齿轮毛坯。

branches.en: ONE OBJECT AND MANY: a single gear and a million bottles are the same making at two scales.
branches.cn: 一个与许多：一枚齿轮与一百万只瓶子，是同一种制作的两个规模。

branches.en: BUILDING A UNIT: fitting parts into a machine and an organ making a substance both assemble a whole.
branches.cn: 组成整体：把零件装成机器与器官合成物质，都在组成一个整体。

branches.en: MAKING WITHOUT MATERIAL: a false alibi and a churned-out song are made with words and speed rather than substance.
branches.cn: 不以材料制作：假的不在场证明与批量炮制的歌，用言辞与速度而非材料做成。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT AS A NOUN: made goods become a class in trade statistics.
branches.cn: 产物成为名词：制成品在贸易统计中成为一大类。

branches.en: THE ACTIVITY AS AN INDUSTRY: the uncountable name stands for a whole trade.
branches.cn: 活动成为行业：不可数名称代表整个行业。

intro.en: Manufacture is a Latin phrase compressed into one French word: a noun for hand, a verb for making, and the ending that carries it into English.
intro.cn: 这是一个被压缩成一个法语词的拉丁短语：一个表示「手」的名词、一个表示「做」的动词，以及把它带进英语的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus gives manual, manage and manuscript; facere gives factory, fact and fabrication; together they name work made by hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「手」的词衍生出手动的、经营与手稿等词；表示「做」的动词衍生出工厂、事实与制作等词；两者合起来指用手做成的工作。

items.example: The hand is the instrument in the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 在这个短语里，手是工具。

items.structure: facere, feci, factum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb carries the action of making.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词承载「制作」的动作。

items.example: The phrase is the source of the whole word.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是整词的来源。

items.example: French fused the phrase into a single noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个短语合成一个名词兼动词。

items.example: The ending marks the outcome of the making.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记制作的结果。

items.example: The agent suffix names the firm.
The process suffix removes the doer.
items.exampleCN: 过程后缀去掉了施动者。

items.example: The participle carries both the factory sense and the false one.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词兼带工厂义与虚假义。

definition_zh: 很好地；令人满意地；整齐精细地；得体地
definition_en: in a way that pleases or satisfies; with care and neatness; in a polite and proper manner; or with a fine judgement of detail
core_image: 桌布铺得平直，杯沿擦得亮，勺子摆成一条线
scene: 客人还没到，主人把桌布重新铺了一遍，杯沿一只只擦亮。 She arranged the cups nicely along the edge of the cloth.
sceneCN: 这里 nicely 是「整齐精细地」（第 2 个义项：对排列和细节都讲究）；句意为她沿着桌布边沿把杯子摆得很整齐。图中可辨识物件：桌布、杯沿、勺子。

pos.zh: 很好地；令人满意地；整齐精细地；得体地

derivatives.zh: nicely 的基础形容词，经古法语自拉丁语 nescius 而来，义为「令人愉快的；细致的；得体的」
由 nice 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「令人愉快的性质；和气」
由 nice 加 -ety 构成，义为「细节；微妙之处」

senses.title: In a pleasing or satisfactory way
senses.definition: in a way that gives pleasure or satisfies the people involved
senses.definitionCN: 以让人愉快或让相关人满意的方式
senses.example: The whole plan worked out nicely in the end.
senses.exampleCN: 整个计划最后顺利办成了。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the approving sense of nice, so it presents the result as one people are glad to accept rather than one that is merely correct.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词保留了 nice 的赞许意味，所以它把结果说成让人乐于接受的样子，而不只是勉强正确。

senses.title: With care, order and precision
senses.definition: with careful attention to arrangement, detail or exactness
senses.definitionCN: 对排列、细节或准确度都用心讲究地
senses.example: She arranged the cups nicely along the edge of the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 她沿着桌布边沿把杯子摆得很整齐。
senses.why: The older sense of nice was delicate and precise, and the adverb keeps that craft sense whenever the subject is how something is placed or made.
senses.whyCN: nice 的旧义是精细、讲究，所以只要话题落在东西怎么摆、怎么做，这个副词就仍带着手艺的意味。

senses.title: In a polite and proper manner
senses.definition: in a way that shows good manners and respect for other people
senses.definitionCN: 表现出良好教养和对他人尊重的方式
senses.example: The children behaved nicely while the guests were there.
senses.exampleCN: 客人来的时候孩子们举止很得体。
senses.why: Because the word approves of what fits a situation, it can judge behaviour as fitting, and politeness is the most social kind of fitting.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词赞许「合乎场合」的东西，它就能用来评判举止是否合宜，而礼貌正是最社会化的合宜。

senses.title: With a fine judgement of degree or timing
senses.definition: with a delicate sense of degree, timing or tone, so that the effect is exactly what was wanted
senses.definitionCN: 在分寸、时机或语气上把握得细，使效果恰好合乎所需
senses.example: The pause was nicely judged, just long enough to let the joke land.
senses.exampleCN: 那个停顿拿捏得刚好，正好够让笑话落地。
senses.why: Precision and approval meet here: a nicely judged detail is at once exact and pleasing, which is why writers use the adverb for timing and tone rather than for size.
senses.whyCN: 精细与赞许在这里汇合：拿捏得当的细节既准确又讨喜，所以写作者用它修饰时机和语气，而不修饰大小。

intro.en: Nicely is the adverb of nice, a Latin word for ignorance that French and English slowly turned into praise.
intro.cn: nicely 是 nice 的副词形式；nice 这个拉丁词原本指无知，经法语和英语慢慢变成了赞许。

items.en: Nescius meant not knowing, built from ne-, not, and scire, to know, so the word began as a remark about ignorance.
items.cn: nescius 意为不知道的，由否定成分 ne- 与 scire（知道）构成，所以这个词起点是一句关于无知的评语。

items.en: Old French nice meant foolish, simple or silly, and it carried that judgement across the Channel.
items.cn: 古法语 nice 意为愚笨的、头脑简单的，把这层贬评带过了海峡。

items.en: Middle English nice still meant foolish or wanton, a long way from the compliment it gives today.
items.cn: 中古英语的 nice 仍指愚笨、放纵，与今天这层夸奖相距很远。

items.en: In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the adjective moved through fussy and delicate to refined and precise, and the adverb nicely followed the same path.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪间，这个形容词从「挑剔、纤巧」转到「精致、准确」，副词 nicely 也走了同一条路。

items.en: Modern English keeps the approving senses of pleasant, careful and proper, while the old sense of foolish has disappeared.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了「愉快、细致、得体」这些赞许义，而「愚笨」的旧义已经消失。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same Latin stem of knowing; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of doing something well.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「知道」拉丁词干上的词；近义组收其他表示把事情做好的副词。

entries.definition: Pleasant, careful or proper, the adjective this adverb is built from.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的、细致的或得体的，是这个词的形容词基础。

entries.definition: The quality of being pleasant or kind.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快或和善的性质。

entries.definition: A small, precise detail or a delicate distinction.
entries.definitionCN: 细小而精确的细节，或微妙的区分。

entries.definition: In a good or satisfactory way, the plainest word for doing something right.
entries.definitionCN: 以良好或令人满意的方式，表示「做得好」的最朴素的词。

entries.definition: In a way that is agreeable and gives no offence.
entries.definitionCN: 以令人愉快、不冒犯人的方式。

entries.definition: In an orderly way, with everything in its proper place.
entries.definitionCN: 整齐有序地，各样东西都各在其位。

entries.definition: In a way that suits the situation or the purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 以适合情境或目的的方式。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of ignorance turned into an English adverb by -ly, and its family still carries both the old judgement and the modern approval.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「无知」的形容词，经 -ly 变成英语副词；它的词族仍同时带着旧日的贬评与今天的赞许。

normal.en: The Latin root is ne plus scire, not to know, so nice once meant ignorant and the praise arrived much later.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根是 ne 加 scire，即「不知道」，所以 nice 曾经指无知，夸奖的意思来得很晚。

normal.en: The suffix -ly only turns an adjective into an adverb, so nicely does whatever nice does, applied to the verb.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 只是把形容词变成副词，所以 nicely 做的事就是 nice 做的事，只不过用在动词上。

normal.en: Niceness names the quality and nicety names a fine detail, showing one stem serving both approval and precision.
normal.cn: niceness 指性质，nicety 指细部，可见同一词干同时服务于赞许与精确。

normal.en: Work out nicely is the usual pattern for a result that ends better than expected.
normal.cn: work out nicely 是固定模式，指结果比预想的要好。

normal.en: The word can modify a pause or a judgement because its old sense of delicate still survives in careful writing.
normal.cn: 这个词能修饰停顿或判断，因为「纤巧」的旧义在讲究的文笔里仍然活着。

abstract.en: A word that began as an insult about ignorance now hands out praise, a reminder that approval is often only a fashion away from contempt.
abstract.cn: 一个从「无知」的贬语开始的词如今用来夸人，提醒人：赞许与轻蔑之间常常只隔一阵风气。

abstract.en: Nicely sits between correct and pleasant, describing things that are right in a way people enjoy.
abstract.cn: nicely 站在「正确」与「愉快」之间，形容那些对得让人喜欢的事。

abstract.en: Because it approves of fit, it can judge a pause as easily as a table setting, which shows how one adverb can measure tact.
abstract.cn: 因为它赞许「合宜」，它能评判一个停顿，也能评判一桌摆设，说明一个副词也能衡量分寸。

examples.en: The whole plan worked out nicely in the end.
examples.cn: 整个计划最后顺利办成了。

examples.en: She arranged the cups nicely along the edge of the cloth.
examples.cn: 她沿着桌布边沿把杯子摆得很整齐。

examples.en: The children behaved nicely while the guests were there.
examples.cn: 客人来的时候孩子们举止很得体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈斯利」——事情办得漂亮，人人都喊一声「奈斯」；记住 nicely 是很好地。

root: nice 源自拉丁语 nescius（不知道的，由 ne-「不」与 scire「知道」构成），经古法语 nice（愚笨的）进入英语；中古英语仍指愚笨、放纵，十六至十七世纪转为「精细、讲究、讨人喜欢」，加 -ly 成副词 nicely。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is doing something in a way people are glad to accept; it divides into neat precision, proper behaviour and fine judgement of timing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把事情做得让人乐于接受；由此分出整齐精细、举止得体，以及分寸拿捏得细。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth smoothed flat, cup rims polished and spoons lined up in a row.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌布铺得平直，杯沿擦得亮，勺子摆成一条线。

branches.en: a plan that ends better than expected
branches.cn: 结果比预想更好的计划

branches.en: spoons lined up at equal distances
branches.cn: 间距相等排成一行的勺子

branches.en: cups turned so all the handles face one way
branches.cn: 杯柄统一朝向摆放的杯子

branches.en: children sitting still while guests talk
branches.cn: 客人说话时坐得端正的孩子

branches.en: a pause held just long enough for a joke
branches.cn: 为笑话留得刚好的停顿

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of ignorance turned into an English adverb by -ly, and its family still carries both the old judgement and the modern approval.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「无知」的形容词，经 -ly 变成英语副词；它的词族仍同时带着旧日的贬评与今天的赞许。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective nescius and its root scire supply the oldest layer, and the adverb ending was added in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 nescius 及其词根 scire 提供最老的一层，副词词尾则是在英语里加上的。

definition_zh: 起源；起点；出身；来源；原点
definition_en: the point at which something begins, the source from which it comes, or the fixed point of a coordinate system
core_image: 一条河从山间石缝里冒出第一股水，往下越流越宽
scene: 山谷尽头，向导蹲下身，指着石缝里冒出的第一股水，说明这条河从这里开始。 The origin of the river lies in a spring high in the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里指「事物开始出现的地点或起点」（第 1 个义项：时间与空间上的开端）；句意为这条河的源头在高山中的一处泉水。图中可辨识物件：石缝、泉水、山谷、向导的手；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 起源；起点；出身；来源；原点

senses.title: The point where something begins
senses.definition: the place or moment at which something first exists or starts
senses.definitionCN: 某物首次存在或开始的地点或时刻
senses.example: The origin of the river lies in a spring high in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河的源头在高山中的一处泉水。
senses.why: origo in Latin meant 'a beginning, a rising', from oriri 'to rise', so the word pictures something rising into existence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 origo 意为「开端、升起」，来自 oriri「升起」，因此这个词把事物想象为升起来而存在。

senses.title: Ancestry and social background
senses.definition: a person's family background or the place a family comes from
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的家庭背景或家族来处
senses.example: Her origin was a small farming village in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她的出身是北方一个小农村。
senses.why: a family's beginning is its first known place, so the word moved from places to people.
senses.whyCN: 家族的起点就是它最早可考的地方，于是这个词从地点移到了人身上。

senses.title: Source or provenance of a thing
senses.definition: the place or process a product or material comes from
senses.definitionCN: 产品或材料所来自的地方或过程
senses.example: The label records the origin of every bean in the bag.
senses.exampleCN: 标签记录袋中每颗豆子的原产地。
senses.why: trade needed a word for where goods begin their journey, and the general sense supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 贸易需要一个词来指货物开始旅程的地方，泛义正好提供了它。

senses.title: The origin of coordinates
senses.definition: the fixed point where the axes of a coordinate system meet
senses.definitionCN: 坐标系各轴相交的固定点
senses.example: The graph starts at the origin and rises to the right.
senses.exampleCN: 图像从原点开始，向右上升。
senses.why: mathematics borrowed the word for the zero point from which all positions are measured.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用了这个词，指一切位置由之量起的零点。

senses.title: The attachment point of a muscle
senses.definition: the end of a muscle that stays fixed when it contracts
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉收缩时保持不动的那一端
senses.example: The muscle's origin is on the pelvis and its insertion on the thigh.
senses.exampleCN: 这块肌肉的起点在骨盆，止点在大腿。
senses.why: anatomy reused the idea of a beginning for the fixed end from which a muscle acts.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把「开端」的观念用于肌肉发力的固定端。

senses.title: Etymology of a word
senses.definition: the earlier form and language from which a word derives
senses.definitionCN: 一个词所由来的更早形式与语言
senses.example: The dictionary gives the origin of the word in Latin.
senses.exampleCN: 词典给出这个词在拉丁语中的来源。
senses.why: a word's history begins somewhere, and that beginning is literally its origin.
senses.whyCN: 一个词的历史总有个开始，而那个开始字面上就是它的 origin。

senses.title: The first cause of an event
senses.definition: the earliest cause that set a chain of events going
senses.definitionCN: 启动一连串事件的最早原因
senses.example: Investigators traced the fire to an origin in faulty wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 调查者把火灾追溯到有问题的线路。
senses.why: causes form chains, and the first link is naturally called the origin.
senses.whyCN: 原因构成链条，第一环自然被称作 origin。

senses.title: Figurative root or source
senses.definition: a borrowed use for the deepest source of a feeling, problem or custom
senses.definitionCN: 借指情感、问题或习俗的最深根源
senses.example: The origin of their quarrel was a careless remark years before.
senses.exampleCN: 他们争吵的根源是多年前一句无心的话。
senses.why: the physical starting point became the image for whatever lies beneath a visible effect.
senses.whyCN: 物理起点成了可见结果之下一切东西的意象。

intro.en: Origin comes from Latin origo 'beginning, source', from oriri 'to rise'. It entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: origin 来自拉丁 origo「开端、来源」，后者出自动词 oriri「升起」，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oriri meant 'to rise, arise', used of the sun and of anything coming into being. Its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: oriri 意为「升起、出现」，用于太阳与任何开始存在的事物。其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Origo, originis meant 'a beginning, a source, a birth', and supplied the whole family of English words.
items.cn: origo, originis 意为「开端、来源、诞生」，提供了英语整组同族词。

items.en: Old French origine carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of a source or birth.
items.cn: 古法语 origine 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指来源或诞生。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word named the zero point of coordinate axes.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个词指坐标轴的零点。

items.en: Anatomy adopted origin for the fixed end of a muscle, extending the family into medicine.
items.cn: 解剖学采用 origin 指肌肉的固定端，把词族扩展到医学。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Latin source of oriri is not established, and any Indo-European root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：oriri 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike nouns built on the same stem; group two holds near-meaning source words.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干构成的形近名词；第二组是语义相近的来源词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'first' or the first version of a work; origin is the starting point itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「最初的」的形容词，或作品的最初版本；origin 是起点本身。

entries.definition: To begin or to bring something into being; it names the event, not the point.
entries.definitionCN: 开始或使某物产生；它指事件，而非那个点。

entries.definition: The quality of being new and inventive; it has moved far from the sense of a beginning.
entries.definitionCN: 新颖而有创造性的品质；已远离「开端」之义。

entries.definition: The process of coming into being; origin is the point, origination is the process.
entries.definitionCN: 产生的过程；origin 是那个点，origination 是过程。

entries.definition: The place, person or thing from which something is obtained; it stresses supply rather than first existence.
entries.definitionCN: 获得某物的地点、人或物；强调供给，而非首次存在。

entries.definition: The first part or first moment of anything; it is the everyday equivalent of origin.
entries.definitionCN: 任何事物的最初部分或最初时刻；是 origin 的日常对应词。

entries.definition: The underlying cause or base of something, often figurative, as the root of a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的深层原因或基础，常为比喻，如问题的根源。

entries.definition: The place where a person or movement was born; it is concrete and geographical.
entries.definitionCN: 人或运动诞生之地；具体且地理性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oriri 'to rise' plus -go gives 'a rising, a beginning'.
normal.cn: oriri「升起」加 -go 即「升起、开端」。

normal.en: The family runs origin, originate, original, originality, originator.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 origin、originate、original、originality、originator。

normal.en: Country of origin is a fixed trade phrase.
normal.cn: 原产国是固定的贸易短语。

normal.en: The origin of coordinates is the zero point of the axes.
normal.cn: 坐标原点是各轴的零点。

normal.en: Anatomy uses origin for the fixed end of a muscle.
normal.cn: 解剖学用 origin 指肌肉的固定端。

abstract.en: Picture the first thread of water coming out of a rock.
abstract.cn: 想象第一缕水从岩石缝里冒出来。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree whose lowest branch is a village.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树，最下面的枝条是一个村庄。

abstract.en: Picture a quarrel that began with one careless sentence years ago.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争吵，始于多年前一句无心的话。

examples.cn: 这一习俗的起源已经失传。

examples.en: The map marks the origin of every shipment.
examples.cn: 地图标出每批货物的来源地。

examples.cn: 图像在零点穿过原点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ori（升起）+ gin（开端）」——事物升起来的那个点 → 起源、起点

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rising point: where a thing begins, where a family begins, where goods come from, the zero of axes, the fixed end of a muscle, a word's history, the first cause and the hidden root.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个「升起的点」：事物开始处、家族开始处、货物来处、坐标零点、肌肉固定端、词的历史、最初原因与隐藏根源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first thread of water rising out of a rock and widening into a river.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一缕水从石缝里升起，逐渐变宽成一条河。

branches.en: BEGINNING AND CAUSE: the first moment and the first cause share one shape.
branches.cn: 开端与原因：最初时刻与最初原因共享同一形状。

branches.en: FAMILY: a person's beginning is a place and a lineage.
branches.cn: 家族：人的开始既是地点，也是血脉。

branches.en: PROVENANCE: goods and words both come from somewhere.
branches.cn: 来源：货物与词都从某处来。

branches.en: FIXED POINTS: axes and muscles need a point that does not move.
branches.cn: 固定点：坐标轴与肌肉都需要一个不动的点。

branches.en: ROOT: the hidden source beneath a visible effect.
branches.cn: 根源：可见结果之下的隐藏来源。

intro.en: Origin is a Latin noun whose stem recurs through a large English family.
intro.cn: origin 是一个拉丁名词，其词干贯穿一大组英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Oriri 'to rise' gives origo, originis and the English family origin, originate, original and originality.
latinIntro.cn: oriri「升起」给出 origo、originis，以及英语同族 origin、originate、original 与 originality。

items.example: The sun is said to rise with this verb.
items.exampleCN: 太阳「升起」就用这个动词。

items.example: Origo is the direct source of origin.
items.exampleCN: origo 是 origin 的直接来源。

items.example: The origin of the word is Latin.

items.example: The practice originated in the north.
The site was originally an orchard.
Her originality showed in every page.
items.exampleCN: 她的独创性在每一页都显现。

items.example: The originator of the method is unknown.
items.exampleCN: 这一方法的创始者不明。

items.example: The word describes peoples from the beginning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词描述「从一开始就在」的民族。

definition_zh: 阶段；时期；月相；相位；相；分阶段实施；逐步引入或淘汰
definition_en: a distinct stage in a process or cycle; the state a regularly changing system has reached at a given moment; to carry something out in planned stages
core_image: 月亮走完一圈，被切成一块块叫得出名字的明暗形状
scene: 工程进入最后阶段，由真实用户试用这套软件。 The project moved into its final phase, when real users test the software.
sceneCN: 这里 phase 是「长过程中的一段」（第 1 个义项：阶段）；句意：项目进入最后阶段，由真实用户测试软件。场景要点：时间轴被切成几段、最后一段、用户试用；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 分阶段实施；使（系统）同步

derivatives.zh: 分阶段的；按计划逐步进行的

senses.title: A stage in a process
senses.definition: one distinct part of a process that has several successive parts
senses.definitionCN: 一个有先后多个环节的过程中，界限清楚的其中一段
senses.example: The first phase of the trial focuses on safety.
senses.exampleCN: 试验的第一阶段重点关注安全性。
senses.why: The word starts from the moon: its endless cycle is cut into named segments. Any long human process is cut the same way, so one segment is a phase.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起于月亮：月亮无休止的循环被切成一段段有名字的形状。人类的任何长期过程也被同样地切开，于是一段就是一个 phase。

senses.title: A period with a shared character
senses.titleCN: 时期：一段有共同特征的岁月
senses.definition: a period in a person's life or in history that has a particular character
senses.definitionCN: 个人生活或历史中具有某种共同特征的一段时间
senses.example: As a teenager he went through a rebellious phase.
senses.exampleCN: 十几岁时他经历过一段叛逆期。
senses.why: Here the slice is marked off not by an external schedule but by shared mood or behaviour. The boundary is drawn by likeness, not by a plan.
senses.whyCN: 这里的切片不是由外部日程划出的，而是由共同的情绪或行为划出的。界线由相似性决定，而非计划。

senses.title: The moon's apparent shape
senses.titleCN: 月相：月亮露出的那张脸
senses.definition: the shape of the moon or another planet as it appears to us at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 月亮或其他行星在某一时刻呈现给我们的形状
senses.example: A thin crescent is the phase just after the new moon.
senses.exampleCN: 细细的蛾眉月是新月之后的那个月相。
senses.why: This is the literal source. Greek phasis means appearance, and the moon is the thing whose appearance changes most visibly night after night.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义来源。希腊语 phasis 意为“显现”，而月亮正是夜复一夜外观变化最明显的那个东西。

senses.title: Physics: position in a wave cycle
senses.titleCN: 相位：波走到一圈的哪个位置
senses.definition: the point that a wave or oscillation has reached in its repeating cycle, measured as an angle
senses.definitionCN: 波或振动在重复循环中到达的位置，用角度来量度
senses.example: The two signals are in phase, so their peaks arrive together.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个信号同相，所以它们的波峰同时到达。
senses.why: A cycle can be drawn as a circle. Where you stand on that circle is your phase, so the moon idea becomes a measurable coordinate.
senses.whyCN: 一个循环可以画成一个圆。你站在那个圆上的位置就是相位，于是月亮的意象变成了可测量的坐标。

senses.title: Chemistry: a distinct state of matter
senses.titleCN: 相：同一条件下的一个物质状态
senses.definition: a state of matter, such as solid, liquid, or gas, that is distinct from other states present in the same system
senses.definitionCN: 同一体系中与其他状态明显不同的物质状态，如固、液、气
senses.example: Ice floating on water is a two-phase system.
senses.exampleCN: 浮在水上的冰构成一个两相体系。
senses.why: Inside one state the material is uniform, like one face of the moon. Crossing a visible boundary puts you in another phase.
senses.whyCN: 在同一个状态内部，物质是均匀的，就像月亮的同一张脸。越过一条可见的界线，就进入了另一个相。

senses.title: To carry out in planned stages
senses.titleCN: 分阶段实施：把整件事拆成几段来办
senses.definition: to organize an activity or change so that it happens in a series of planned stages
senses.definitionCN: 把一项活动或变革组织成一系列按计划推进的阶段
senses.example: The company will phase the new software into its offices over six months.
senses.exampleCN: 公司将在六个月内把新软件分阶段引入各个办公室。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: you treat a process as named slices and then perform the slices one at a time.
senses.whyCN: 名词动用：把过程当成一片片有名字的切片，再一片一片地执行。

senses.title: To introduce or remove gradually
senses.titleCN: 逐步引入／淘汰：一段一段地来
senses.definition: to bring something in or take it out gradually, stage by stage, instead of all at once
senses.definitionCN: 不是一次性，而是逐阶段地引入或撤出某物
senses.example: The old buses were phased out and replaced by electric ones.
senses.exampleCN: 旧公交车被逐步淘汰，换成了电动车。
senses.why: Phase in and phase out differ only in direction. Both keep every step small so that no single change is disruptive.
senses.whyCN: phase in 与 phase out 只差方向。两者都把每一步做小，使任何单次变化都不至于造成震荡。

senses.title: One aspect of a larger thing
senses.titleCN: 侧面：事物露给人的那一面
senses.definition: one part or aspect of a situation, especially the part that shows at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 一个情况的某一部分或某一方面，尤指某一时刻显露出来的那一面
senses.example: They studied only one phase of the problem, ignoring its economic side.
senses.exampleCN: 他们只研究了问题的一个侧面，忽略了其经济面。
senses.why: Phasis is appearance. Whatever shows itself at a given moment is one face of a larger object that has other faces.
senses.whyCN: phasis 是“显现”。在某一刻显现出来的，总是一个更大事物的其中一张脸，它还有别的脸。

intro.en: Phase began as an astronomer's word for the moon's changing face. From there it spread to any cycle cut into stages, and finally to any aspect of anything.
intro.cn: phase 起初是天文学家用来称月亮变换的脸的术语。由此扩及任何被切成阶段的循环，最后泛指任何事物的一个侧面。

items.en: Phainein meant 'to show, bring to light'. It comes from PIE *bha- 'to shine', the same family that gives English beacon and the Greek root behind phenomenon and emphasis.
items.cn: phainein 意为“显现、带到光下”。它来自原始印欧语 *bha-“发光”，同族词包括英语 beacon，以及 phenomenon、emphasis 背后的希腊词根。

items.en: From phainein came phasis, 'appearance', used especially of a star or the moon showing itself. The noun describes the act of appearing and the shape that appears.
items.cn: 由 phainein 生出 phasis“显现”，多用于星辰或月亮出现在天空中。这个名词既指显现的动作，也指显现出来的形状。

items.en: Greek astronomers spoke of the phases of the moon because its visible shape changes in a regular cycle. The term was technical before it was general.
items.cn: 希腊天文学家说月亮的 phases，因为它的可见形状按固定周期变化。这个词先是专业术语，后来才泛化。

items.en: Latin took phasis as a learned borrowing from Greek, keeping its astronomical sense. English received it through this Latin channel rather than directly.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 phasis 作为学术借词从希腊语引入，保留了天文学含义。英语是经这条拉丁渠道而非直接从希腊语接手的。

items.en: Phase of the moon is recorded in the 1660s. The general sense 'stage of development' appears in the 19th century, and the physics sense of wave phase follows in the same period.
items.cn: phase of the moon 的用法记录于 17 世纪 60 年代。“发展阶段”的泛义出现在 19 世纪，物理学上的“波相位”也同期出现。

items.en: Chemistry adopted phase for a distinct state of matter, and engineering adopted phase in and phase out for staged change. All of them keep the original picture: a cycle sliced into named parts.
items.cn: 化学用 phase 指一种独立的物质状态，工程领域用 phase in／phase out 指分阶段变更。这些用法都保留了原初画面：一个循环被切成有名字的几份。

note.en: The first group is built on near-identical spelling, only one of which shares the Greek root. The second group collects words for stages and aspects, each from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组拼写相近，其中只有一个与希腊词根同源。第二组收表示“阶段、方面”的词，但各自角度不同。

entries.definition: a group of words that forms a unit. It comes from Greek phrasis 'expression', from phrazein 'to point out, explain', not from phainein.
entries.definitionCN: 由一组词构成的单位。它来自希腊语 phrasis“表达”，动词 phrazein“指出、说明”，并非来自 phainein。

entries.definition: a rotating vector used to represent a wave, named directly from phase plus the -or agent ending.
entries.definitionCN: 用来表示波的旋转矢量，直接由 phase 加表施动者的 -or 构成。

entries.definition: arranged or carried out in stages. It is the past participle of the verb phase used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 按阶段安排或实施的。它是动词 phase 的过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: the gradual removal of something, formed from the verb phrase phase out.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步撤除某物，由动词短语 phase out 构成的复合名词。

entries.definition: a point or period in a process. Stage stresses the level reached, while phase stresses the bounded slice and often implies a cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 过程中的一个点或一段。stage 强调达到的程度，phase 强调有界的切片，且常含周期性。

entries.definition: a length of time with a defined beginning and end. Period is purely about time; phase also carries the idea of a distinct state or stage.
entries.definitionCN: 有明确起点和终点的一段时间。period 只谈时间；phase 还带有“独立状态或阶段”的意思。

entries.definition: one action in a sequence. A step is what you do; a phase is the stretch of time in which you do it.
entries.definitionCN: 序列中的一个动作。step 是你做的动作；phase 是做这件事的那段时间。

entries.definition: one part or feature of a situation. Aspect fits sense 08 closely; both come from roots meaning 'to look'.
entries.definitionCN: 情况的一个部分或特征。aspect 与第 8 义项最贴近，两者词根都含“看”的意思。

entries.definition: the condition something is in at a given time. State is static; phase is a position within a changing cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 某物在某一时刻所处的状况。state 是静态的；phase 是变化循环中的位置。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks: the moon, the sliced timeline, the in/out pair, the synchronized waves, and the face behind the Greek word.
normalIntro.cn: 五个具体抓手：月亮、被切分的时间轴、进与出的一对、同步的波、以及希腊词背后那张脸。

normal.en: PHASE = the moon's face. Picture eight named moons hanging on a string.
normal.cn: PHASE＝月亮的脸。想象八个有名字的月亮挂在一条绳上。

normal.en: Take a long timeline and cut it into thick slices. Each slice has a name; each name is a phase.
normal.cn: 把一条长长的时间轴切成厚片。每一片都有名字，每个名字就是一个 phase。

normal.en: Phase in: slices come in from the left. Phase out: slices leave to the right.
normal.cn: phase in：切片从左边进来；phase out：切片从右边退出。

normal.en: In phase means two waves raise their hands at the same moment. Out of phase means one is early.
normal.cn: in phase 是两个波在同一刻举手；out of phase 是一个来早了。

normal.en: Phase and face are cousins in meaning: both are about what shows. The moon changes face; we name its faces as phases.
normal.cn: phase 与 face 在意思上是亲戚：都关乎“显现出来的样子”。月亮换脸，我们把这些脸命名为 phase。

abstract.en: Any long thing can be treated as a circle cut into arcs; naming an arc is already a theory of the whole.
abstract.cn: 任何漫长之物都可以被看成切成弧段的圆；给一段弧命名，本身就已经是对整体的理论。

abstract.en: A phase is a frozen frame from a film that never stops running.
abstract.cn: 一个 phase 是从一部永不停机的电影里截下来的一帧。

abstract.en: Boundaries between phases are drawn by observers, not found in nature; the cycle only becomes usable when we cut it.
abstract.cn: 阶段之间的界线是观察者画的，不是自然里现成的；只有切开，循环才变得可用。

examples.en: The negotiation entered a delicate phase after both sides had stated their positions.
examples.cn: 双方陈述立场之后，谈判进入了一个微妙的阶段。

examples.en: Engineers check that the two generators remain in phase before connecting them to the grid.
examples.cn: 工程师在把两台发电机接入电网前，要确认它们保持同相。

examples.en: The city plans to phase out diesel buses by 2030, replacing them route by route.
examples.cn: 这座城市计划到 2030 年逐步淘汰柴油公交，按线路逐条替换。

dict_mnemonic.text: “费兹”听起来像 face（脸）——月亮一夜换一张脸，换出的每张脸就是一个 phase（月相、阶段）

root: 希腊语 phainein“显现、照亮”→ phasis“显现（月相）”→ 拉丁 phasis → 英语 phase；与 phenomenon、emphasis、fantasy 同一条 phan- 线。

sensesIntro.en: Start from the moon and move outward: one visible shape, then one stretch of a cycle, then one stretch of any process, then one aspect of anything. The verb adds the idea of doing the slices one at a time.
sensesIntro.cn: 从月亮出发向外推：先是一个可见形状，再是一个循环中的一段，再是任何过程的一段，最后是任何事物的一个侧面。动词义则加上“一片一片地做”的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full moon cycle divided into named arcs, each arc showing a different face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整轮月相循环被切成有名字的弧段，每段露出不同的脸。

chain: A CYCLE CUT INTO NAMED SLICES
ONE SLICE FROZEN AT A MOMENT

branches.en: TIME: a slice of a process and a stretch of life share one boundary-drawing gesture.
branches.cn: 时间：过程的一段与人生的一段，共用同一个划界动作。

branches.en: MOON: the literal origin, the visible face that gave the word its name.
branches.cn: 月亮：本义来源，那个让这个词得名的可见的脸。

branches.en: SCIENCE: wave position and state of matter both turn the slice into a measurable coordinate.
branches.cn: 科学：波的位置与物质状态，都把切片变成可测量的坐标。

branches.en: ACTION: doing the slices in order, inward or outward.
branches.cn: 行动：按顺序做这些切片，向内引入或向外撤出。

branches.en: ASPECT: whatever shows at one moment is one face of a larger thing.
branches.cn: 侧面：某一刻显现出来的，总是更大事物的其中一张脸。

intro.en: The phase family is built on one Greek verb of showing, with prefixes that locate the showing (above, through) and suffixes that turn it into nouns and adjectives.
intro.cn: phase 词族建立在一个表示“显现”的希腊动词上，前缀标明显现的位置（在上、穿过），后缀把它变成名词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed these Greek forms whole, so the same pieces appear in Latin scientific vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把这些希腊形式整体借入，所以同样的构件也出现在拉丁科技术语里。

definition_zh: 轻微的；纤细的；轻视
definition_en: small in degree, thin in build, or to treat someone without respect

scene: 她的声音里有一丝轻微的颤抖。 There was a slight tremble in her voice.

senses.title: Small in degree
senses.definition: small in amount, degree, or importance
senses.definitionCN: 数量、程度或重要性很小
senses.example: There was a slight tremble in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音里有一丝轻微的颤抖。
senses.why: This is the main everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的主要义项。

senses.title: Thin in build
senses.definition: thin and not strongly built
senses.definitionCN: 瘦小且不强壮
senses.example: A slight figure waited by the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一个瘦小的身影在门口等候。
senses.why: A small body looks slight.
senses.whyCN: 小小的身体看起来瘦弱。

senses.title: Treat without respect
senses.definition: to treat someone as if they are not important
senses.definitionCN: 把某人当作不重要的人对待
senses.example: He felt slighted by the short reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他因那简短的回覆而感到被怠慢。
senses.why: The adjective's smallness became an act of ignoring.
senses.whyCN: 形容词的「小」引申为忽视的行为。

intro.en: Slight probably came from an old word for smooth or level.
intro.cn: slight 可能来自表示光滑或平坦的古老词。

items.en: Slettr meant smooth or level.
items.cn: slettr 意为光滑或平坦。

items.en: The word appeared as slight.
items.cn: 这个词以 slight 的形式出现。

items.en: It came to mean thin or small.

items.en: The sense of unimportant grew.
items.cn: 「不重要」的义项发展起来。

items.en: As a verb it meant to ignore or insult.
items.cn: 作动词时意为忽视或怠慢。

normalIntro.en: Slight means small enough to miss, in body or in manner.
normalIntro.cn: slight 意为小到容易忽略，无论身体还是态度。

normal.en: Do not worry about a slight delay.

abstract.en: To slight someone is to make them small in your eyes.

abstract.en: Small differences decide large outcomes.

sensesIntro.en: Slight means small in degree, thin in body, or an act of treating someone as unimportant.
sensesIntro.cn: slight 意为程度轻微、身体瘦弱，或轻视某人的行为。

core.en: Small enough to be almost unnoticed.

branches.en: What is treated as small can also hurt.

intro.en: Slight forms words for small amounts and small insults.

latinIntro.en: Slight is Germanic in origin, not Latin.

definition_zh: 奖；奖品；授予；判给
definition_en: a prize given for achievement, or to give such a prize officially
core_image: 一只奖杯被递到伸出的双手上
scene: 典礼上掌声响起。 The judge awarded her the first prize.
sceneCN: 这里 award 是「授予」（第 2 个义项：正式把奖项或款项给某人）；句意是评委把一等奖授予了她。

derivatives.zh: 由 award 加 -ee 构成，义为「获奖者」
由 award 与 winning 复合而成，义为「获奖的；屡获殊荣的」

senses.title: A prize
senses.definition: something given to someone for an achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因成就而发给某人的东西
senses.example: She received an award for her research.
senses.exampleCN: 她因研究成果获得了一个奖项。
senses.why: Award comes from Old French eswarder, to judge, so a prize is what a judge decides to give.
senses.whyCN: award 来自古法语 eswarder「评判」，所以奖项就是评判者决定给出的东西。

senses.title: Give officially
senses.definition: to give money or a prize officially
senses.definitionCN: 正式发给钱款或奖项
senses.example: The judge awarded her the first prize.
senses.exampleCN: 评委把一等奖授予了她。
senses.why: The noun for a decided gift turned into the verb for the deciding and giving.
senses.whyCN: 表示判定给予之物的名词，转成了表示判定并给予的动词。

senses.title: Decide legally
senses.definition: to decide that someone should receive money in a court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上裁定某人应得钱款
senses.example: The court awarded damages to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判给这家人损害赔偿金。
senses.why: A judge's decision is the oldest sense, and the courtroom is where the giving is most formal.
senses.whyCN: 评判者的裁定是最古老的义项，而法庭正是这种给予最正式的场合。

intro.en: Award is a word about judging before it is a word about prizes.

definition_en: a regular sum of money given for a purpose, pocket money, a permitted amount, a tax-free amount, a price reduction, or the act of taking something into account

scene: 机场值机柜台前，行李箱刚放上秤，指针就超出了刻度。 Her suitcase was five kilos over the baggage allowance.
